name: mint-mac-care
title: Mint - Mac Storage Cleanup for You and Your Agents
description: Optimize and clean up Mac storage for you and your AI agents: caches, Xcode builds, duplicate files and the gigabytes Codex, Claude Code and Cursor keep
author: dzg-studio

commands.name: mint-status
commands.title: View Mac Status
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Disk space, memory and organized folders at a glance, with their Auto Care, like Mint's menu bar

commands.name: mint-optimize
commands.title: Optimize Storage
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Get space back without deleting anything: identical copies share their storage, by source like Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and your files

commands.name: mint-scan
commands.title: Free Disk
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Free disk space: share identical copies, clean the caches, logs and build output apps make again, and choose from your own files

commands.name: mint-organize
commands.title: Organize a Folder
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: How many loose files each folder has to sort and where they go, then tidy it in one step

commands.name: mint-memory
commands.title: Free Memory
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Quit idle apps to free RAM in one step, or choose which apps to quit

commands.name: mint-uninstall
commands.title: Uninstall App
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Find an app and what it left behind, then move them to the Trash

commands.name: mint-undo
commands.title: Undo Mint Action
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Restore eligible files from recent Mint operations while files and recovery records remain available

commands.name: mint-why
commands.title: Show Disk Growth
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: What grew on your disk this week, by app, folder, category or AI tool

tools.name: get-disk-overview
tools.title: Get Disk Overview
tools.description: How full the Mac's disk is and what Mint found at its last Scan, in four groups: Optimizable (identical copies that can share their storage, nothing deleted), Safe to clean (caches, build output and leftovers that apps make again), Yours (the person's own files, chosen one by one) and Keep. Read-only.

tools.name: get-memory-overview
tools.title: Get Memory Overview
tools.description: How much memory is in use and which apps hold it, in Mint's piles: Idle (Mint would quit these by itself), In use and Ask first, each app sized by what quitting it gives back. Read-only.

tools.name: get-disk-growth
tools.title: Get Disk Growth
tools.description: What grew on the Mac's disk over the last days, by app or folder and by category, from the maps Mint keeps after each Scan. Read-only.

tools.name: open-mint-command
tools.title: Open Mint Command
tools.description: Open one of Mint's commands in Raycast (Free Disk, Optimize Storage, Free Memory, Organize a Folder, Uninstall App, Show Disk Growth or View Mac Status) so the person reviews what it would do and confirms it there. The tool itself changes nothing.

ai.instructions: Mint must be installed for these tools to answer; if a tool says it is not, pass on its words and link. The read tools never change anything. Mint never removes, quits or moves anything from an AI answer: when the person wants space or memory back, say what Mint found with its sizes, then open the matching command with open-mint-command so they review and confirm it there. Never say something was cleaned, freed or deleted. Optimizable gives space back without deleting any file; Safe to clean is what apps make again; Yours is the person's own files. Write sizes exactly as the tools give them.

evals.input: @mint what's taking up space on my Mac?
@mint how much space can I get back without deleting anything?
@mint which apps are using the most memory right now?
@mint what grew on my disk this week?

mocks.open-mint-command: Opened Free Disk. Nothing has changed yet: the person reviews it there and confirms.

scripts.validate: npm run lint && npm test && npm run build
scripts.prepublishOnly: echo 'Publish this extension through the Raycast Store, not npm.' && exit 1
